tagline: An old highway alignment reaches Brighton Beach on the May River
intro: Alljoy Road, S-7-13, follows the former SC 46 alignment to Brighton Beach. It forms the final leg of the May River Scenic Byway: South Carolina’s code designates S-13 from S-66 to Brighton Beach on the May River. The full byway combines sections of SC 46, S-66 and S-13, totaling approximately eleven miles.

SC 46 originally continued south from Bluffton to Brighton Beach. In 1956, the highway turned north and then east toward the Hilton Head ferry, leaving the beach alignment as Alljoy Road. The 2012 act established the May River Scenic Byway and repealed the earlier 1978 Beaufort County scenic-highway act. The drive on S-13 runs from the S-66 junction to Brighton Beach at the river.

moments.title: The S-66 junction
moments.text: The designated S-13 segment begins at its intersection with S-66. The May River Scenic Byway reaches this junction by following S-66 from SC 46 in Bluffton.

moments.title: The former SC 46 alignment
moments.text: Alljoy Road was the southern end of SC 46’s route through Bluffton to Brighton Beach. The highway’s 1956 rerouting took SC 46 toward the Hilton Head ferry, and the old beach road became S-7-13.

moments.title: Brighton Beach
moments.text: Brighton Beach on the May River is the endpoint named in the state’s May River Scenic Byway designation. It was also the endpoint of SC 46 before the 1956 change through Bluffton.

sources.label: South Carolina Legislature, Code of Laws: Title 57, Chapter 23, Scenic Highways
